content.comment_body: Hello. I connected an encoder (one channel, HTL output) to the input I4 on the [product_name] [version_no] base module, but it seems to be acting as a standard input rather than a fast one. Impulses are registered only when the encoder rotates very slowly. My test diagram is shown below. Is there anything additional I should check to get the high-speed counter (HSC) working correctly?

Can you estimate the pulse frequency where the issue occurs? The maximum pulse frequency this [product_name] can handle is 5kHz. What voltage do you measure with your multimeter when the encoder outputs pulses at high speed? Note that this version does not support fast inputs.
Actually, this base module supports fast inputs. Please see the attached PDF for reference.
In the screenshot, it appears you have connected the Z-signal to Input I5 and linked I5 to the reset input on the counter. Try running the setup without the reset connection.
Apologies, I confused the [version_no] with the [version_no]. Thank you, [user_name]. What do you think could be causing this user's issue?

analysis.insight_summary: The user is experiencing difficulty with encoder pulses being counted accurately by the [product_name] [version_no] base module. Specifically, pulses are only registered at low speeds, suggesting the fast input or high-speed counting function is not behaving as expected. There is some misunderstanding among users regarding which module versions support fast inputs.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the input on the [product_name] [version_no] to reliably register fast pulses and operate as a high-speed counter, not just at slow speeds. They assume fast input functionality is supported and are seeking advice or clarification on how to achieve proper HSC operation.
